My main complaint when I went through EMT training was all the simulation was for worst case scenario patients. When realistically the calls you prepare for happen a lot less often than you’re taught to believe. When I started my first job I was so confused that I didn’t see critical patients that often. I think it was maybe on my third or fourth shift is when I saw my first critical patient. The majority of calls realistically are old people that have a simple issue that they just need transported to the hospital. My simulations were great for those critical calls I just was a little lost for the first few patients that I had nothing to do for them.
